When a circuit breaker detects that a component is overloaded, it trips and shuts off the circuit, stopping power to the affected area. This prevents the overload from causing damage to the equipment or causing a fire.

Circuit breakers are commonly used in homes, businesses, and industrial settings to protect against electrical overloads and ensure safe operation of electrical systems.
